s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal mass with chronic vomiting and right upper-quadrant pain
salient_findings: Large, firm, palpable mass in the right upper quadrant
Large retroperitoneal mass with fatty and soft-tissue components
key_facts: 2-year history of intermittent vomiting
Right upper-quadrant pain
Sensation of fullness on the right side of the abdomen
Denies urinary symptoms or changes in bowel habits
History of heavy menstruation and iron deficiency anemia
Oral iron therapy for over 10 years
Beta-thalassemia trait on hemoglobin electrophoresis
Hemoglobin levels ranging from 6 to 10 g/dL
Abdominal ultrasonography showed a well-defined hyperechoic heterogeneous mass
Contrast-enhanced CT showed a well-defined, encapsulated retroperitoneal lesion
MRI confirmed a large right retroperitoneal predominantly fatty mass

shortlist.label: Myelolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large right retroperitoneal predominantly fatty mass with soft-tissue nodular areas

shortlist.label: Adrenal myelolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location in the hepatorenal space and fatty density on CT

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Heterogeneous mass with areas of soft-tissue density on CT and MRI

shortlist.label: Retroperitoneal teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Complex mass with both fatty and soft-tissue components

shortlist.label: Adrenal cortical carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large size and encapsulated nature of the mass with displacement of adjacent organs

raw.rationale: The presence of a large, well-defined, encapsulated retroperitoneal lesion with mostly fat density and internal areas of soft-tissue density, as seen on CT and MRI, is consistent with myelolipoma. The patient's beta-thalassemia trait and history of anemia may also contribute to the development of myelolipoma, which is a benign tumor composed of adipose tissue and hematopoietic elements.

rejected.label: Liposarcoma
rejected.why: Liposarcoma is a malignant tumor and would likely show more aggressive features on imaging, such as invasion of adjacent organs, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Retroperitoneal teratoma
rejected.why: Retroperitoneal teratoma would typically contain a mix of different tissue types, including cystic and solid components, which is not consistent with the predominantly fatty mass seen on imaging.

rejected.label: Adrenal cortical carcinoma
rejected.why: Adrenal cortical carcinoma would likely show more aggressive features on imaging, such as invasion of adjacent organs, and would not typically have a predominantly fatty composition.

rejected.label: Adrenal myelolipoma
rejected.why: While adrenal myelolipoma is a possible diagnosis, the location of the mass is described as retroperitoneal, which is not specific to the adrenal gland, making myelolipoma a more general and appropriate diagnosis.
